chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'I have committed adultery, so purify me.' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) turned his face away from him. He came to him from his other side and said the same thing, and he turned his face away from him again. Then he came a third time and said to him: 'O Messenger of God! I have committed adultery, and the punishment of this world is easier for me than the punishment of the Hereafter.'

So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) asked: 'Is there something wrong with your companion?' — meaning insanity. They said: 'No.' So he confessed against himself for the fourth time. Then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) ordered that he be stoned, and they dug a pit for him. When he felt the touch of the stones, he fled running fast. Al-Zubayr encountered him and threw a camel's leg-bone at him, so he fell and was restrained by it. Then the people caught up with him and killed him.

They informed the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) of that, so he said: 'Why did you not leave him alone?' Then he said: 'Had he concealed himself and then repented, that would have been better for him.'

key_terms.اسْتَتَرَ: Concealed himself — Islamic legal principle that hiding one's sins from authorities is permissible and sometimes encouraged
key_terms.تَابَ: Repented (tawbah) — private repentance directly to God, deemed superior to public legal punishment
key_terms.فَطَهِّرْنِي: Purify me (by executing the prescribed punishment, thus expiating the sin before God)
key_terms.يُرْجَمَ: Be stoned — the hadd punishment for adultery when proven by confession or four witnesses

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet do when a man confessed adultery and asked to be purified by stoning?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq narrates a hadith in which a man confesses adultery to the Prophet and asks for the prescribed purification (ritual execution by stoning). The Prophet initially averts his face — reflecting the Islamic principle that rulers and judges are not required to pursue hidden sins — and only proceeds with the legal penalty after four explicit confessions, the minimum required by Shia fiqh. The Prophet's statement that the man should have concealed his sin and repented privately reveals the higher spiritual priority of sincere repentance over legal punishment in Islamic ethics. This hadith belongs to the chapter on the description of stoning (al-rajm), a capital punishment prescribed for proven adultery in classical Islamic law.
